translation_loss.what_was_lost: The specific mythological weight of 'cheerharan' (the public disrobing of Draupadi in the Mahabharata assembly) is translated as a generic 'disrobing', losing the immediate cultural and epic resonance of the original event.

The shift from the specific divine names 'Govind' and 'Krishna' to their English transliterations loses the immediate cultural recognition of these names as epithets of the same deity who historically rescued Draupadi.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The feminine verb endings 'banogi' and 'chunogi' explicitly mark the subject's gender in Hindi, reinforcing that Draupadi herself must act. This grammatical gender marking is lost in the gender-neutral English verbs 'become' and 'choose'.

original_poem:
सुनो द्रौपदी शस्त्र उठा लो,  
अब गोविन्द ना आएंगे।  
तुम्हारे इस चीरहरण पर,  
कोई कृष्ण नहीं आएंगे।  

ये ध्वंस, धूल, ये रज कण,  
बस केवल तुम्हारे ही साथी होंगे।  
न्याय और धर्म की मर्यादा को,  
तुम्हें स्वयं ही साकार करना होगा।  

इस संग्राम के अंधकार में,  
तुम्हीं अपनी ज्योति बनोगी।  
अब शक्ति तुम्हारे ही हाथों में है,  
तुम्हीं अपना पथ चुनोगी।
translated_poem:
Listen, Draupadi, take up arms,  
For Govind will not come.  
In this disrobing of yours,  
No Krishna will arrive.  

This ruin, this dust, this handful of soil,  
Will be your only companions.  
The dignity of justice and dharma,  
You alone must embody.  

In the darkness of this battle,  
You shall become your own light.  
The power now rests in your hands,  
You alone will choose your path.
